_meta.description: Published India sector market sizes, used to anchor national/online TAM. Replaces figures that were hard-coded inline in ml_service.py with no source attached.
_meta.definition: total_market_inr_cr is the PUBLISHED TOTAL market for the sector in India. addressable_share is the fraction an early-stage venture can realistically compete for; the app sizes TAM as total_market_inr_cr * addressable_share, so a new entrant is not shown the whole national market as if it were reachable.
_meta.addressable_share_rationale: addressable_share is the one judgment in this file: the published totals are real, the fraction a new venture can reach is not published anywhere. Each sector now carries a share_rationale naming the actual barrier - RBI licensing, clinical licensing, RMG licensing, utility-scale incumbency - rather than a number chosen to preserve earlier output. Sectors still marked low confidence carry no published total at all. Logistics is the strongest case in the file: its share is not reasoned at all but anchored to a separately published sub-segment - express and courier at Rs 78,525 crore - so 0.0375 reproduces a printed figure to within 0.1%. Only cybersecurity now carries no published total.

fields.total_market_inr_cr: Published total India market size, INR crore.
fields.addressable_share: Planning assumption: fraction reachable by an early-stage entrant.
fields.source: Publication the total is taken from.
fields.confidence: high = named published figure; medium = derived from a published adjacent figure; low = planning assumption with no published India figure found.

ecosystem_context.source: Inc42 Datalabs, Indian Tech Startup Funding Report H1 2025
ecosystem_context.note: Tier-1 cities took 92.8% of H1 2025 funding; Tier-2 and Tier-3 together took 2.5%. Relevant to any venture outside a metro that plans to raise.

fx_inr_per_usd.source: Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India (FEDAI), reproduced in IBEF sector reports, May 2026
fx_inr_per_usd.note: Every USD figure is converted at the rate for the year that figure describes, not a single flat rate. A flat Rs 83.5/USD was previously used throughout and was wrong by up to 4.2% against the 2025 rate of Rs 87.16.
fx_inr_per_usd.coverage: Calendar years 2015-2026 and fiscal years 2022-23 to 2026-27. The 2015-2021 calendar rates were added because the Indian startup funding dataset spans 2015-2020 and was previously converted at a flat Rs 87/USD - a rate from 2025 applied to deals up to a decade older, overstating the rupee figures by 17-36%.

_meta.known_inconsistency_share_basis: Two different bases are in use and they are not equivalent. Most sectors set addressable_share as a CAPTURE FRACTION - roughly what one early-stage venture could compete for, which is what the definition above describes. Logistics instead sets it as SEGMENT ADDRESSABILITY: express and courier is 3.75% of the logistics total, so 0.0375 is the size of the layer a startup can operate in, not the slice one startup would win. The logistics figure is the better-evidenced of the two because it reproduces a published number, but it answers a different question. Gaming could be put on the same segment basis today - its detail block already carries the FY24 split showing a free-to-play studio addresses roughly US$1.3bn of US$3.8bn, about 0.34 against the 0.06 currently set - which would raise its TAM around 5.7x. That change is NOT made here because switching one more sector to the segment basis without switching all of them would deepen the inconsistency rather than fix it. Resolving this means choosing one basis for the whole file and restating the definition to match.

ecommerce.source: IBEF, India Brand Equity Foundation - E-commerce (Rs 10,82,875 crore / US$125bn)

funding_h1_2025.source: Inc42 Datalabs, Indian Tech Startup Funding Report H1 2025
funding_h1_2025.note: Capital deployed into Indian startups in this sector, not market size.

ecommerce.share_rationale: Highly fragmented with low regulatory barrier; a niche or category entrant can take a real slice.

fintech.source: IMARC / Mordor Intelligence - India fintech market US$155.67bn (2025), converted at the CY2025 FEDAI rate of Rs 87.16/USD

funding_h1_2025.source: Inc42 Datalabs, Indian Tech Startup Funding Report H1 2025
funding_h1_2025.note: Capital deployed into Indian startups in this sector, not market size.

fintech.share_rationale: RBI licensing (payment-aggregator authorisation, KYC, capital adequacy) is a hard gate. Most of this market is closed to an unlicensed entrant.

healthcare.source: IBEF - India healthcare industry projected US$650bn by 2030; 2025 mid-point interpolation of US$325bn, converted at the CY2025 FEDAI rate of Rs 87.16/USD

funding_h1_2025.source: Inc42 Datalabs, Indian Tech Startup Funding Report H1 2025
funding_h1_2025.note: Capital deployed into Indian startups in this sector, not market size.

healthcare.share_rationale: Clinical licensing and capital intensity restrict entry; most spend goes to established hospitals and pharmacy chains.

edtech.source: IAMAI + Grant Thornton Bharat - Indian edtech market Rs 64,875 crore (US$7.5bn), via IBEF Education & Training, May 2026

funding_h1_2025.source: IBEF Education & Training, May 2026 (Rs 1,071 crore across 11 deals, a fivefold rebound)
funding_h1_2025.note: Capital deployed into Indian edtech startups in this sector, not market size.

edtech.share_rationale: Low regulatory barrier to entry, but the segment is consolidating hard - upGrad signed a term sheet to acquire Unacademy in March 2026 and PhysicsWallah listed at a 33-42% premium in November 2025. A new entrant competes against funded incumbents, not open field.
edtech.corroboration: Statista independently puts India's online education market at Rs 65,458 crore (US$7.57bn) for 2025 - within 0.9% of the IAMAI figure. Two different methodologies, same answer.

detail.note: The Rs 58,088 crore coaching industry is the relevant figure for a physical coaching centre; the Rs 64,875 crore edtech figure is for an online product. They are different markets.

gaming.source: Lumikai x Google, 'Levelling up: State of India Interactive Media & Gaming FY24' (Nov 2024) - US$3.8bn in FY24, converted at the FY2023-24 FEDAI rate of Rs 82.80/USD

detail.note: Only 25% of gamers pay. Paying users, not installs, are the addressable base.

segment_split_fy24_usd_bn.note: Real-money gaming is 63% of the market and is a licensed, 28%-GST segment a new studio cannot simply enter. A free-to-play or premium studio addresses in-app purchases plus ads, roughly US$1.3bn (Rs 10,855 cr), not the headline US$3.8bn. Lumikai also reports RMG gross-to-net margin down 30% and user-acquisition payback doubled under the new GST regime.

gaming.share_rationale: Real-money gaming is 63% of the market, licensed and taxed at 28% GST. A free-to-play studio addresses in-app purchases plus ads only.

logistics.source: IMARC / Economic Survey - India logistics market US$240.5bn (2025), converted at FEDAI Rs 87.16/USD for calendar 2025, via IBEF Infrastructure, May 2026

funding_h1_2025.source: Inc42 Datalabs, Indian Tech Startup Funding Report H1 2025
funding_h1_2025.note: Capital deployed into Indian startups in this sector, not market size.

logistics.share_rationale: The US$240.5bn total is freight and warehousing spend across road, rail, air, ocean and 3PL - overwhelmingly bulk movement on long-term contracts held by incumbents, plus port and rail capex a startup cannot address at all. The layer that is genuinely open to a new entrant is express logistics and courier, which the same report sizes at Rs 78,525 crore for FY25. That is 3.75% of the total, so the share is set to 0.0375 and reproduces the published express figure rather than being reverse-engineered from a target output.
logistics.corroboration: Two independent checks. (1) The share is anchored to a separately published sub-segment figure, not assumed: 0.0375 x Rs 20,96,198 crore = Rs 78,607 crore against the published Rs 78,525 crore, 0.1% apart. (2) Converting the express segment's own US$9bn at the FY2024-25 FEDAI rate of Rs 86.47 gives Rs 77,823 crore against IBEF's printed Rs 78,525 crore - 0.89% apart, confirming the rupee figures and the FX table agree to under one percent.

detail.note: The FY30 express projection (US$18-22bn) is a forecast and is deliberately NOT used as the market size; total_market_inr_cr stays on the measured 2025 figure.

cleantech.source: MNRE / IBEF Renewable Energy, May 2026 - the 500 GW by 2030 target carries an investment opportunity of US$221bn, annualised across 2026-2030 and converted at the FY2025-26 FEDAI rate of Rs 88.37/USD

funding_h1_2025.source: Inc42 Datalabs, Indian Tech Startup Funding Report H1 2025
funding_h1_2025.note: Capital deployed into Indian startups in this sector, not market size.

cleantech.measures: ANNUAL CAPITAL DEPLOYMENT into renewable projects, not consumer spending. Unlike the other sectors here, this sector's market is capital formation - state that plainly wherever it is shown.
cleantech.share_rationale: Utility-scale is dominated by NTPC (Rs 2 lakh crore committed in Madhya Pradesh alone), Adani, ReNew (Rs 82,000 crore in Andhra Pradesh) and JSW. A startup does not compete for those projects. 2% reflects the distributed and services layer a new entrant can actually reach.
cleantech.corroboration: Moody's independently estimates US$190-215bn for the same 500 GW target over 2023-2030, plus US$150-170bn for transmission and storage - consistent with the US$221bn figure.

rooftop_solar_addressable.note: PM Surya Ghar rooftop solar is the segment a small cleantech venture can realistically serve: 40 lakh households reached against a one-crore target, so roughly 60 lakh households remain. Utility-scale is not addressable by a startup.

agritech.source: IMARC / Bain & Co. - India smart agriculture market US$860.7mn (2025), converted at FEDAI Rs 87.16/USD for calendar 2025, via IBEF Agriculture and Allied Industries, May 2026

funding_h1_2025.source: Inc42 Datalabs, Indian Tech Startup Funding Report H1 2025
funding_h1_2025.note: Capital deployed into Indian startups in this sector, not market size.

agritech.share_rationale: Share is 1.0 here for a different reason than a placeholder: the US$860.7mn figure already measures only the technology layer - precision agriculture, sensing, advisory and farming-as-a-service - so it is an addressable market as published, not a total to take a slice of. It is deliberately NOT the Rs 56,08,471 crore agriculture GVA, which measures farm output; a startup selling software to farmers does not address the value of the crop.
agritech.corroboration: No second independent source was found for the smart-agriculture total, which is why this is medium and not high. The figure is directionally supported by the sector's funding: Inc42 records US$143mn deployed across 16 agritech deals in H1 2025, roughly 17% of the measured annual market - a ratio consistent with an early, under-penetrated category rather than a mature one.

detail.note: agri_gva and agri_credit are context only and are NOT fed to the models or used as a TAM. They measure farm output and lending, not addressable spend on agritech products. The previous placeholder of Rs 30,000 crore overstated this market by 4.0x.

cybersecurity.source: PLANNING ASSUMPTION - no current published India cybersecurity total was confirmed.
cybersecurity.share_rationale: PLANNING ASSUMPTION - no published India total confirmed for this sector.
cybersecurity.addressable_share_note: share is 1.0 because total_market_inr_cr here is NOT a published market total - it is a directly-assumed addressable figure carried over from the old inline code. There is no real total to take a share of. Replace both together when a published India figure is found.

_default.source: PLANNING ASSUMPTION - generic sector default, no published figure.
